meta.crawl_scope: All indexable marketing and legal routes from sitemap.xml. App routes, admin and /i/ invite links are noindex by design and were excluded from content scoring but tested for header correctness.
meta.rendering: Headless Chromium via Playwright. Raw HTML captured separately for every route and for 10 distinct crawler user agents.

summary.business_type: Pre-launch consumer mobile and web application (social planning / group coordination), audience 15-22, free to users with a venue-side B2B model
top_findings: Every AI crawler tested (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Amazonbot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bingbot) received an identical 2880-byte document with an empty body, because the site is client-rendered and none of them execute JavaScript. Googlebot renders and sees all 818 words of the homepage. Mitigated by llms.txt and static JSON-LD; the root cause needs prerendering.

The homepage claims two venue features that are on the Not built list in CLAUDE.md: promoted placement in vote lists (LandingPage.js:792) and slow-night push offers (LandingPage.js:794). This is an accuracy failure in a card whose CTA is a sales mailto.
Zero structured data existed anywhere on the site. Now fixed at site level with Organization, WebSite and WebApplication; FAQPage on /support is still missing.
Six of seven indexable pages inherited the homepage meta description, so /privacy described itself to searchers as being about voting on bars and splitting bills.

Six places across four files assert a team headcount and a moderation response SLA that contradict AboutPage.js describing a solo student founder. Two of them are commitments an App Store reviewer will read.
quick_wins: Delete the two unshipped venue feature bullets from LandingPage.js (two lines).
Repoint five internal links from /landing to / (one line in each of five files).
Add a meta description write to the existing useEffect in six files; copy is already drafted in the handoff.
Reword four statement-shaped support headings as questions, then wrap the existing 7 Q&A pairs in FAQPage JSON-LD.
Tick TASKS.md:274-279, which still lists the shipped invite preview function as an open TODO.
verified_working_no_defect: Invite link previews. The UA-conditional rewrite fires for facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot, Slackbot, Discordbot, WhatsApp, Applebot and the real iMessage user agent; humans get the React app at the same URL. The success path produces 'Sarah invited you to Friday Night Out' with date, venue and going count. REACT_APP_API_URL is unset in Vercel and that is correct: the hardcoded fallback is the live Railway backend. Failures always return 200 with generic tags and are never cached. Escaping is applied to every user-authored value. The two copies of the bot regex in vercel.json are byte-for-byte identical.

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Per-route canonicals served as HTTP Link headers from vercel.json rather than a single static link tag that would have collapsed all seven pages onto the homepage
HTTPS with HSTS max-age 63072000, apex 308-redirects to www
Full security header set on every route: X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, CSP frame-ancestors, Permissions-Policy
Private routes use X-Robots-Tag noindex rather than robots.txt Disallow, which keeps link previews working on /i/ while keeping the URLs out of the index
Valid sitemap.xml, 7 URLs, all returning 200 and canonical-consistent
Brotli on HTML, JS and CSS; immutable caching on hashed static assets

findings.title: Site is invisible to crawlers that do not execute JavaScript
findings.description: The raw HTML body for every route is a noscript tag and an empty div. Ten AI and search crawler user agents were tested live and all received the same empty 2880-byte shell. Googlebot renders JavaScript and is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Prerender the seven marketing routes to static HTML at build time. Mitigated in the interim by llms.txt and static JSON-LD, both of which are in the raw head.

findings.title: Duplicate raw-HTML title and description across all 7 indexable URLs
findings.description: One index.html serves every route. React corrects the title per route after hydration, so Googlebot resolves unique titles, but no non-rendering crawler does, and six of seven descriptions are never corrected at all.
findings.recommendation: Add per-route description writes (handoff item 3), and fix at the root with prerendering.

findings.title: No llms.txt
findings.description: GET /llms.txt returned 200 with the SPA shell, because the catch-all rewrite swallowed it. A crawler looking for the file received HTML pretending to be it.
findings.recommendation: FIXED. frontend/public/llms.txt created, 4329 bytes, pure ASCII, served as text/plain.

findings.title: AI crawler policy was implicit rather than decided
findings.description: User-agent: * / Allow: / permitted every AI crawler by omission.
findings.recommendation: FIXED. robots.txt now names answer-time and training crawlers in separate groups, with the reversal path documented and a warning that named groups replace rather than stack with the wildcard group.

findings.title: Soft 404s on every unknown URL
findings.description: The catch-all rewrite at vercel.json:239 returns HTTP 200 for any path that does not exist. src/index.js:472 sets a Page not found title client-side but the status stays 200.
findings.recommendation: Deferred. Needs a catch-all serverless function in the rendering path for every route, which is disproportionate while the site has almost no inbound links. Fold into the prerender work.

findings.title: Stale documentation claiming the invite preview function did not exist
findings.description: The Open Graph comment block in public/index.html stated that api/invite-preview.js and the UA-conditional rewrite did not exist. Both ship and were verified working.
findings.recommendation: FIXED. Comment rewritten to record the verified behaviour and the fallback contract.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Zero banned register words across the entire shipping copy: no seamless, effortless, unlock, leverage, elevate, streamline or personalize your experience
Zero em dashes in user-visible text, zero emoji as icons, zero fake testimonials, no purple gradients, no scroll-reveal animations
All five numeric crowd-model claims on /about verified true against backend/scripts/ml/models/model_metadata.json
Privacy policy is 3195 words and names 15 subprocessors; terms have 11 numbered sections
Real human byline, and source comments show copy discipline is actively maintained rather than accidental

findings.title: Homepage claims two features that are not built
findings.description: LandingPage.js:792 claims promoted placement in vote lists and :794 claims slow-night push offers. Both appear on the Not built list in CLAUDE.md and both are Boost-tier features in backend/routes/venueDashboard.js:38. The card's CTA is a sales mailto.
findings.recommendation: Delete both bullets, or apply the same 'Venue tools are in development' hedge AboutPage.js:113-114 already uses.

findings.title: Team size and moderation SLA contradict the founder description
findings.description: SupportPage.js:25 and :90, DeleteAccount.js:86-87, TermsOfService.js:66-68 and CommunityGuidelines.js:115 all say we or our team and promise triage cadence, while AboutPage.js:122-123 describes a solo student founder. The Terms and Guidelines instances are moderation commitments an App Store reviewer will read.
findings.recommendation: Pick one voice. For a solo founder, 'I read every message' is both truer and a stronger trust signal.

findings.title: Authoritativeness is close to zero
findings.description: No social profiles exist anywhere in the source. No App Store listing (404 as of 2026-08-14), no Product Hunt, no Crunchbase, no press. The only third-party credential is a DECA placement stated twice with no year and no link.
findings.recommendation: Human steps H4, H5, H8, H9. This is the ceiling on all GEO work.

findings.title: /about and /support are thin
findings.description: 513 and 393 words. /about is the page an answer engine is most likely to want, has no image, and carries the only verifiable proof points on the site.
findings.recommendation: Expand /about, add a product image, state the DECA credential with a year.

findings.title: No non-product content of any kind
findings.description: No blog, comparison page, glossary or location page. Nothing on the domain could rank for how to plan a night out with friends.
findings.recommendation: Defensible pre-launch, but make it an explicit decision. Three or four genuinely useful pages beat twenty thin ones.

findings.title: Synthetic numbers rendered as plain text
findings.description: LandingPage.js:686-692 renders a $116.82 bill split with five named people, and :729-739 renders an SOS email mock captioned 'The actual email'. Both are indistinguishable from real data to a text extractor.
findings.recommendation: Add a visually-hidden Example label.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every page has exactly one h1 and there are zero heading-level skips across all seven pages
Every link is a real anchor element; no onClick-only pseudo-links anywhere
The landing menu panel stays in the DOM with only a CSS class toggling visibility, so a crawler sees all six menu links
Canonicals are correct on all seven URLs

findings.title: Six of seven pages inherit the homepage meta description
findings.description: Only LandingPage.js:241-242 writes a description. /privacy currently describes itself as being about voting on where to go and splitting the bill.
findings.recommendation: Add a description write to the existing useEffect in each of six files. Copy drafted in HANDOFF-frontend-src.md item 3.

findings.title: Five internal links point at /landing, a non-canonical duplicate
findings.description: SupportPage.js:19 and :104, PrivacyPolicy.js:107, TermsOfService.js:16, CommunityGuidelines.js:22, DeleteAccount.js:25. AboutPage.js already uses / correctly.
findings.recommendation: Change all five to /.

findings.title: No navigation on any subpage
findings.description: The six subpages emit between zero and three internal links each; CommunityGuidelines.js emits exactly one and does not link to /privacy or /terms despite TermsOfService.js:31 declaring the guidelines part of the Terms. The landing footer is the only full nav on the site.
findings.recommendation: Extract the LandingPage.js:862-899 footer into a shared component and mount it on all seven routes.

findings.title: IntersectionObserver gating may hide the live demo from crawlers
findings.description: LandingPage.js:127-164 gates LiveDemo and both BirdieBird instances behind an observer. The non-observer fallback does not help because Googlebot's renderer has IntersectionObserver. This sits directly below the page's boldest claim at :559-561.
findings.recommendation: Raise rootMargin substantially or render the demo's textual content unconditionally.

findings.title: Inconsistent title delimiter and thin subpage titles
findings.description: Pipe on / and /i/, middot on the six subpages. 'About - Flock' is 13 characters with no topic token.
findings.recommendation: Standardise the delimiter and add a topic modifier to subpage titles without stuffing.

findings.title: No per-route Open Graph tags
findings.description: Sharing /about or /privacy shows the homepage card. Invite links are correctly excepted and handled by api/invite-preview.js.
findings.recommendation: Fold into the prerender work.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: Organization, WebSite and WebApplication now present as a single @graph with @id cross-references anchored to the homepage
Verified to survive the production build and parse as valid JSON
No fabricated ratings, review counts, download counts or interaction counts

findings.title: No structured data existed anywhere on the site
findings.description: render_page.py reported structured_data.block_count 0 on the homepage, and a grep for ld+json, schema.org and itemprop across all of frontend/ returned nothing.
findings.recommendation: FIXED at site level in public/index.html. Only site-level entities were added, because that file is the response for every route.

findings.title: FAQPage markup missing on /support
findings.description: Seven hand-written Q&A pairs already exist as h3 followed by p, including 'How does the budget feature stay anonymous?' which no competitor page can duplicate. Four of the seven are phrased as statements rather than questions.
findings.recommendation: Reword the four statements as questions, then inject FAQPage JSON-LD from SupportPage.js. It must not go in index.html, which would claim /privacy and /terms carry the same questions.

findings.title: sameAs and MobileApplication deferred until the App Store listing is live
findings.description: Apple ID 6781442127 is real but the store URL returns 404 today, and LandingPage.js:43 keeps APP_STORE_LIVE false for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: Add sameAs, a MobileApplication entity and iOS in operatingSystem in the same change that flips that flag.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: Main JS bundle is 67.6 KB brotli and the build is code-split into many small chunks
CSS is 10.9 KB brotli; fonts are self-hosted rather than CDN-loaded
No analytics tag or third-party script in the head; Sentry and PostHog are dynamic imports gated on env keys
Immutable year-long caching on hashed static assets, revalidating HTML
The decision not to preload the hero screenshot is documented and correct: the LCP element was measured as the h1 at all four tested widths

findings.title: No field data was obtainable
findings.description: CrUX and PageSpeed Insights need a Google API key; Search Console needs domain verification. Neither is available in this environment, so this score is inferred from asset weights and caching rather than measured from real users.
findings.recommendation: Human step H3. Treat 80 as provisional until PageSpeed Insights is run against the live URL.

findings.title: Client-side rendering delays first paint
findings.description: Inherent to the CRA architecture. First paint waits on JavaScript download, parse and execute.
findings.recommendation: Prerendering the marketing routes fixes this and the crawler visibility problem in the same change.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: llms.txt now carries the full product description rather than a link index, because the rendered body is unreachable to non-JS crawlers
Static JSON-LD reaches non-rendering crawlers on every route
robots.txt now records the training-versus-citation decision explicitly

findings.title: AI crawlers received an empty document
findings.description: Ten crawler user agents tested live, all HTTP 200, all with an empty body. For those crawlers the entire knowable content of flockcorp.com was one title and one meta description.
findings.recommendation: Mitigated by llms.txt and JSON-LD. Root cause needs prerendering.

findings.title: No brand mention or entity corroboration signals
findings.description: No sameAs anywhere. No Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, Product Hunt or App Store entry. Flock is also a heavily contested brand name, which makes entity disambiguation harder than usual. The website is currently the only source that says Flock exists.
findings.recommendation: Human steps H4, H5, H8, H9. Almost none of this is code.

findings.title: Strongest citable passages are the least reachable
findings.description: The budget-anonymity answer on /support and the verified crowd-model paragraph on /about are the most citable content on the site. Both are client-rendered, neither has schema, and four of the seven support questions are phrased as statements.
findings.recommendation: Both are now summarised in llms.txt as the fastest available path to citability. Reword the headings and add FAQPage.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Every marketing image has an alt attribute; decorative images correctly use empty alt with aria-hidden
Content images have genuinely descriptive alt text
Intrinsic width and height on every marketing image, so no CLS from these pages
WebP with PNG fallback via picture on the hero and Birdie screenshots
og-image.png is genuinely 1200x630 as declared; all icon files match their declared sizes, verified by reading the files

findings.title: Roughly 2 MB of unreferenced legacy screenshots ship in the deploy
findings.description: frontend/public/screenshots/ contains discover.png at 455 KB, crowd.png, chat.png, split.png and six others with no WebP siblings, alongside the app-nest and app-birdie pair that appear to be live.
findings.recommendation: Confirm they are unused (some may be referenced from App.js) and delete. Repo hygiene call for the src/ owners.

findings.title: BirdieBird images have no intrinsic dimensions
findings.description: components/ui/BirdieBird.js:641, 660, 680. CLS is covered by an aspectRatio box in the WhenNear hold prop, which works but is fragile.
findings.recommendation: Add width and height attributes.

findings.title: One lazy image missing decoding and fetchPriority
findings.description: LandingPage.js:582-588 is the only lazy image on the page without decoding async and fetchPriority low, inconsistent with the file's own pattern.
findings.recommendation: Match the other three.

findings.title: Image filenames carry no keywords and /about has no image
findings.description: app-nest.png, mark-steps-400.png and similar will not surface in image search.
findings.recommendation: Low priority pre-launch.

Verified with CI=true npm run build

Tick TASKS.md:274-279, which still lists the shipped invite preview as a TODO

human_steps: H1: Verify www.flockcorp.com in Google Search Console by DNS TXT, then submit the sitemap. Highest-value human step; no indexation or field data was measurable without it.
H2: Verify in Bing Webmaster Tools. Bing powers ChatGPT web search, so this matters more than usual here.
H3: Run PageSpeed Insights on / and /about, mobile profile. The performance score in this audit is inferred, not measured.
H4: Create Instagram and TikTok profiles, then add them to Organization.sameAs.
H5: When Apple approves the app, flip APP_STORE_LIVE in LandingPage.js:43, add sameAs, add a MobileApplication entity and add iOS to operatingSystem, all in one change.
H6: Decide the AI training question. robots.txt currently allows both training and answer-time crawlers and documents how to disallow only training.
H7: Confirm whether the bird cutouts and the mark illustrations are AI-generated. SLOP-AUDIT Section M bans AI-generated photography and no provenance is recorded in the repo.
H8: Add a year and a resolvable link to the DECA credential.
H9: Consider a Product Hunt or equivalent listing for entity corroboration.
not_attempted: DataForSEO, Moz and Ahrefs data (keyword volumes, SERP positions, backlink profiles, competitor gaps) require paid API keys that are not present
Google Search Console, PageSpeed Insights, CrUX field data and GA4 organic traffic require a Google Cloud project or domain verification
Common Crawl domain-level metrics were not run
No competitor comparison was performed; without SERP data it would be guesswork
